name: Model and Amateur Rocketry
summary: Hands-on rocketry for beginners: building and flying model and high-power rockets safely under the NAR and Tripoli safety codes and aviation rules.

topics.name: Model rocket anatomy: body tube, nose cone, fins, launch lug, recovery system
Commercial motors: impulse classes (A to O), thrust curves and motor designations
Stability: finding CG and CP, the Barrowman method and the one-caliber rule
Flight simulation with OpenRocket or RockSim
Recovery systems: parachutes, streamers, dual deploy, ejection charges and altimeters
NAR Model Rocket Safety Code and High Power Rocket Safety Code
Tripoli Rocketry Association safety code and high-power certification levels (L1 to L3)
Launch site setup: range safety officer, launch controllers, pads and standoff distances
Airspace regulations: FAA Part 101 and waivers (and national equivalents)
Avionics for hobby rockets: flight computers, telemetry and GPS tracking
Experimental and research motors: why propellant making requires training and licensing
Student competitions: Spaceport America Cup, TARC, and university rocketry teams
Amateur liquid-fuel and sounding rocket projects and their safety culture
